description: We are high school students from Turkey.We love doing projects. We like coding,designing and presenting our projects.
summary:
Earth in Every Sense is a data sonification and accessibility-first web platform created for the Jukebox challenge, designed to empower blind and visually impaired (BVI) individuals to experience NASA’s Earth photography and geological structures through sound. Space and Earth sciences rely heavily on visual satellite imagery, creating a sensory barrier for the visually impaired community.

Our project transforms NASA’s Earth observation imagery, elevation maps, and geological datasets into rich, meaningful acoustic landscapes (sonification) paired with structured audio descriptions. By selecting any location on Earth—such as Ankara—users can literally "listen" to the planet's geology and topography. Elevation changes, surface textures, and color spectra from NASA’s orbital photography are mapped to musical notes, pitch, rhythm, and timbre, turning Earth’s geological story into an accessible symphony for everyone, regardless of sight.
details:
1. Alignment with the Jukebox Challenge & Motivation The Jukebox challenge asks us to translate NASA’s scientific data into audio experiences that tell a story. While NASA captures stunning photographs of Earth’s crust, fault lines, craters, and basins, over 285 million visually impaired people worldwide cannot access this visual wonder. Earth in Every Sense turns planetary imagery and geology into an auditory journey, proving that Earth observation can be felt and understood without sight.

2. How It Works: From NASA Pixels & Geology to Sound When a user enters coordinates or selects a location (e.g., Ankara, Türkiye), the platform analyzes regional satellite imagery, Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and geological classifications to generate a multi-layered auditory profile:

  • Topographic & Image Sonification Engine: Pixel brightness, color spectra (representing vegetation, water, rock, or urban zones), and elevation gradients are algorithmically mapped to audio frequencies, harmonic scales, and ambient textures. Steep mountain ridges produce higher pitches and dynamic swells, while flat basins generate deep, steady resonant tones.
  • Geological Audio Storytelling: Alongside the sonified soundscape, a screen-reader-optimized narrative describes the visual composition of NASA’s Earth photography and explains the underlying geological formations (tectonic plates, erosion patterns, volcanic history).
  • Interactive Auditory Scanning: Users can navigate across the terrain using simple keyboard controls to hear real-time acoustic shifts as they move from one geological feature to another.

3. Accessibility & Technical Architecture

  • Zero-Barrier UX (WCAG Compliant): Designed specifically for screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) with full keyboard-only navigation, clear ARIA landmarks, and high-contrast visuals for low-vision users.
  • Web Audio Synthesis: Uses browser-native Web Audio APIs to synthesize real-time, lag-free soundscapes directly from spatial and image parameters without requiring external audio hardware.
